messages:
maria: Heads-up: seeing a spike in GPU OOMs on prod-1 over the last 20m after the kernel-selector change. Affected jobs are the KV-cache warm paths that issue long-prefix queries. Logs show sudden reserved>allocated and fragmentation blips.

ajay: can you paste the nvidia-smi + allocator head logs? also which kernel version did we flip to?

maria: nvidia-smi snapshot: 
```
+------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    |
| GPU 0: A100-SXM4 40GB                               |
+------------------------------------------------------+
| Memory-Usage | 38095MiB / 40960MiB                    |
+------------------------------------------------------+
```
allocator.log excerpt: 
```
[13:04:12] device=0 reserved=38416MiB allocated=37320MiB free_frag=1.8GiB largest_free=512MiB
[13:04:12] alloc failed  (size=768MiB)  retrying with compaction
[13:04:12] compaction: moved 2 blocks, freed=640MiB
[13:04:12] alloc succeeded (size=768MiB) but high fragmentation
```
kernel-selector: rolled to opt-kernel-v2 (sparse-attn optimizations) at ~12:30

sophie: immediate ideas: 1) enable request-shaping on router: cap sequence_len to 1024 and soft-reject >2048, 2) enable fallback model variant with 24GB footprint for heavy KV requests, 3) flip kernel-selector back to v1 if quick rollback possible.

leo: additional quick mitigation: set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6" on the pod's envs to reduce fragmentation pressure. also toggle torch backend flag to prefer_cudamalloc_async=true to reuse freed blocks faster.

maria: applied request-shaping rule to drop sequences >4096 and added fallback to smaller model for 5% of traffic (canary). early signs: OOMs dropped from ~6/min to 1/min.

ajay: for postmortem/profiler: grab a heap snapshot via our allocator probe and kernel perf stat run:
```
# on node
curl -s http://localhost:9200/allocs/dump | jq . > /tmp/alloc_snapshot.json
nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys-prod-kv --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=30s --force
```
include `largest_free` and `total_free` metrics. also capture per-kernel mem footprint: `pytorch_kernels.csv` from the runtime.

sophie: long-term fixes we should prioritize in roadmap: 
- deterministic buffer pool with per-shape freelists (reduce split/merge churn)
- stricter KV cache eviction policy: LRU with size-aware quotas + backpressure signal to router when total cached_bytes > 70% of pool
- workspace sizing per model variant (auto-tune during canary) so kernels don't request oversized workspaces concurrently
- rollback guard in kernel-selector that runs A/B perf checks for fragmentation before enabling globally

leo: prioritized ticket: ALLOC-1937 (allocator: freelist compaction pass + expose max_split_size flag) and KV-1022 (size-aware eviction + router backpressure).

infra-bot: deploy request accepted: rollback kernel-selector -> opt-kernel-v1 (sha: d3f2a1) scheduled on prod-1 in 5m; will route 100% traffic back if health ok.

maria: after rollback and request-shaping, memory headroom increased to ~3.2GiB and fragmentation markers normalized. still watching. will attach profiler dumps to the incident postmortem. thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: follow-up: make sure our canary tests include high-KV prefix lengths (100-200MB cached keys) into perf-regress harness. observed perf/regression correlation with large keysets.

maria: noted. creating the postmortem + changelog entry now.
